headline: Network inference from omics data resolves signaling rewiring in cancer cells
label: Network Inference From Omics Data
summary: Recent preprints and publications apply condition-comparative network models to transcriptomic, phosphoproteomic, proteomic and single-cell data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inferring signaling or interaction networks from omics measurements and comparing them across conditions. The dasatinib-resistance preprint applies a cross-talk network model to resistant pancreatic cancer transcriptomes and flags p53 and FcεRI perturbation and BCL2L1 as features of the resistant state, though it is unreviewed. The EGF benchmark evaluates kinase-kinase pathway inference from phosphoproteomics and kinase-substrate interactions across three new datasets, using literature-curated networks as reference. dominoSignal adds a differential test for ligand-receptor communication across conditions in single-cell data, and BDDN infers time-resolved changes in protein-protein interactions between groups in cancer proteomics. scDock and the Virtual Biotech connect network-derived inputs to docking or multi-agent drug discovery workflows. What is new is the emphasis on dynamic, benchmarked, condition-differential network inference, with inferred structure assessed against curated knowledge or formal statistical testing.
